items.title: 61520_Teddy Edwards oral history interview
items.q: In fact, my Aunt's husband owned The Jackson Advocate, the Black newspaper there before he passed, and she runs it now... But he used to try to get me to come back home.

ctx.x: You know, just whuppin' the guys in the band, and the girls -- everybody. Just started swingin' their billy-clubs.

That's the kind of stuff they used to do down there! It could get pretty wild, with that racial thing down there during those days. They tell me it's much, much better now in general -- in general, you know. Even in Jackson, my people tell me... In fact, my Aunt's husband owned The Jackson Advocate, the Black newspaper there before he passed, and she runs it now... But he used to try to get me to come back home. I'll go there when I can get around to it. But he used to tell me, "Come back, because people want to…

Getting back to the music, I'd like to mention a young man that I'm very proud of. He's Vice President of the college in Meridian, Mississippi. And he had the college band there when he was the band-master. And two years ago he brought his school band to the Junior Rose Bowl out here in Los Angeles, and he came by to see me.
